_about: THE ACANTHUS (Acanthus mollis, bear's breeches): a great clump of glossy, dark, deeply cut leaves arching from the ground -- the leaf carved round every Corinthian capital -- and in summer tall stiff spikes of hooded flowers, white lipped, each under a dusky purple spiny bract, in rows up the stalk. Wild in the Mediterranean's shady places, grown in its gardens since antiquity.
